How Our FedEx Attorney Works to Help You

A FedEx truck accident claim is not like a typical car accident case. FedEx is a large corporation with its own response team, which often reaches the accident scene before the injured party has even spoken to a lawyer. Evidence gets collected, statements get recorded, and the narrative around the crash starts taking shape without you.
Having legal representation early changes everything. As your
Denver FedEx truck accident lawyer
, we step in quickly and take the pressure off your plate entirely:
Protected Evidence:

We send preservation letters immediately and obtain vehicle data, electronic logging device records, driver logs, and maintenance histories before they can be overwritten or destroyed. In FedEx cases, this step alone can determine what is provable.
Full Accountability:

FedEx often tries to distance itself from liability by classifying drivers as independent contractors. We investigate the full employment picture and challenge that classification when the facts support doing so, to ensure the right parties are held accountable.
Handled Communications:
Insurance adjusters work for the other side and are trained to use what you say against you. Once you retain us, you do not speak to them directly. We manage every conversation on your behalf.
Trial-Ready Representation:

Every settlement offer gets measured against your full documented losses. If the number does not reflect what you have actually been through, we are prepared to take it to court and let a jury decide.
Under the
Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations

, commercial carriers like FedEx are held to strict federal standards covering driver conduct, vehicle maintenance, and cargo handling. When those standards are violated and a crash results, that record becomes a foundation of the case against them.
Common Causes of FedEx Truck Accidents in Denver

Denver’s dense traffic corridors, active freight routes along I-25 and I-70, and unpredictable winter weather create a demanding operating environment for any delivery driver. FedEx drivers face some of the most aggressive delivery schedules in the industry, and that pressure shapes behavior on the road in ways that directly increase the risk of a serious crash.
Common causes we see in
Denver FedEx truck accident
cases include the following:
Driver Fatigue:
According to the
National Highway Traffic Safety Administration

, drowsy driving impairs reaction time and judgment in ways that are often indistinguishable from impaired driving. Long delivery shifts with compressed turnaround windows make fatigue a persistent hazard on Denver roads, particularly during early morning and late night routes.
Speeding and Reckless Operation:

Quota pressure pushes drivers to exceed safe speeds, especially in residential neighborhoods and on high-volume arterials. The size and weight of a delivery truck makes this far more dangerous than speeding in a passenger vehicle.
Distracted Driving
GPS navigation, routing updates, and handheld device use are common distractions during active deliveries, pulling a driver’s attention away from the road at critical moments.
Brake and Mechanical Failures:
Inadequate maintenance of brake systems and tires can cause catastrophic loss of control, particularly on steep Denver grades or during emergency stops when reaction time is everything.
Improper Loading:
Unsecured or overloaded cargo shifts during transit and can destabilize a vehicle mid-route, making it difficult or impossible for the driver to maintain control.
Hazardous Weather:
Colorado’s winter conditions, including ice, snow, and reduced visibility, demand adjusted driving practices that overworked drivers under tight deadlines sometimes skip entirely.

Any one of these factors can cause a serious collision, and in many crashes, more than one is at play. Determining exactly what went wrong, identifying who bears responsibility, and gathering the evidence to support those conclusions is where having a
Denver FedEx truck accident lawyer
on your side makes a real difference.
Injuries Common in Delivery Truck Collisions

Taking the right steps after a crash is especially important given how serious these injuries tend to be. Delivery trucks carry significant weight, and the force of a collision with one is far greater than most passenger vehicle occupants anticipate. Injuries sustained in FedEx truck crashes frequently require long-term medical management and can permanently affect a person’s ability to work and live independently.
Among the most serious injuries we see in these cases:
Spinal Cord Injuries
Damage to the spinal cord can result in partial or complete paralysis. According to
MedlinePlus
, spinal cord injuries disrupt the signals between the brain and the body, leading to weakness, loss of movement, and paralysis that may be permanent.
Traumatic Brain Injuries
A hard impact to the head can affect memory, concentration, and cognitive function, with effects that persist long after the initial injury.
Broken Bones and Fractures:
Rib, pelvic, and limb fractures are common when a smaller vehicle collides with a large delivery truck, particularly in side-impact and front-end crashes.
Internal Organ Damage:

Blunt force to the torso can injure the liver, spleen, or kidneys without any visible signs at the scene, making prompt medical evaluation critical even when you feel relatively stable after the crash.
Soft Tissue Injuries:

Whiplash, torn ligaments, and muscle damage often take days to show up but can cause lasting pain and limit mobility for months or longer, sometimes requiring ongoing treatment well after the case is resolved.

Injuries like these do not resolve quickly, and the costs that come with them go well beyond the initial hospital visit. Ongoing treatment, lost work, and permanent limitations all add up over time. Getting a full and accurate picture of those losses before agreeing to any settlement is one of the most important steps in the entire process.
Who Can Be Held Liable for a FedEx Truck Accident in Denver?

One of the most important questions in any FedEx truck accident case is who is actually responsible. The answer is rarely limited to the driver. FedEx and the parties connected to its operations create a web of potential liability, and identifying every responsible party is essential to recovering full compensation.

FedEx Corporation is the starting point in most cases. When a driver operates under FedEx’s direction, follows its routes, and uses its equipment, the company can be held accountable for that driver’s negligence through a legal principle known as vicarious liability. FedEx frequently attempts to avoid this by classifying drivers as independent contractors rather than employees. That classification does not automatically protect them, and we investigate the actual nature of the working relationship to challenge it when the facts support doing so.
Beyond the corporation itself, other parties may share responsibility depending on how the crash occurred:
The Driver:

A driver who was speeding, fatigued, distracted, or in violation of federal rules on the number of hours they can work in a day can be held directly responsible for the crash. In some cases, a driver’s prior violations or complaints against them become part of the evidence.
Vehicle Maintenance Contractors:
If a separate company was hired to service the truck and a mechanical problem contributed to the crash, that contractor may share some of the responsibility.
Cargo Loading Companies:
If the cargo on the truck was packed incorrectly or loaded beyond safe limits, causing the vehicle to become unstable, the company that loaded it may be liable for the resulting damages.
Vehicle or Parts Manufacturers:
If a faulty part, such as a defective brake system or tire, played a role in causing the collision, the manufacturer of that part may face a product liability claim.
Colorado is a fault-based state, which means the party or parties responsible for causing the crash are financially accountable for the resulting harm. Under

, liability can be distributed across multiple defendants, and each party’s share of fault is evaluated separately. Pursuing all responsible parties, rather than just the most obvious one, is often what determines whether a victim recovers full compensation or settles for a fraction of what the case is worth.
What You Should Do After an Accident With a FedEx Truck
Knowing what causes these crashes matters, but what you do in the hours that follow matters just as much. The
decisions made after a FedEx truck collision
directly shape the strength of a claim. FedEx’s response team is experienced, well-funded, and focused on limiting the company’s exposure from the start. Your response needs to match the preparation.
Seek Medical Care Immediately:

Even when symptoms seem minor, prompt evaluation creates a medical record connecting your injuries directly to the crash date. Some injuries, including concussions and soft tissue damage, do not present fully until hours or days later.
Call Law Enforcement:
A police report establishes an independent, contemporaneous record of the scene, the parties involved, and any visible violations. Without one, liability becomes much harder to establish.
Document the Scene:
Photographs of vehicle positions, road conditions, FedEx vehicle markings, and debris all matter later when liability is disputed. If you are unable to do this yourself, ask someone nearby for help.
Do Not Give a Statement to FedEx:
FedEx’s insurance representatives are trained to gather information that minimizes the company’s exposure. Do not say anything beyond what law enforcement requires, even if the request seems routine.
Contact a Denver FedEx Truck Accident Lawyer:
Early legal involvement preserves evidence, prevents costly missteps, and ensures your rights are protected from the start.

, Colorado personal injury claims must generally be filed within three years of the accident date. Evidence fades over time, witnesses become harder to locate, and details become harder to reconstruct. Speaking with the team at
Dormer Harpring
early in the process can make a meaningful difference in how a case develops and what can be proven.
How Much Compensation Can I Receive for My FedEx Truck Accident Case?

There is no fixed amount for a claim related to a FedEx truck accident, and anyone who gives you a number before reviewing your case is guessing. What Colorado law does provide is a clear framework for the categories of loss you are entitled to pursue, and in serious truck accident cases, those categories add up quickly.
Economic damages
cover the financial losses you can document:
Medical bills, both current and those expected in the future
Wages lost while recovering, and any long-term reduction in your ability to earn
Rehabilitation and physical therapy costs
Long-term care needs or assistive equipment required because of your injuries
Non-economic damages cover the personal toll that does not come with a receipt:
Physical pain and ongoing suffering
Emotional distress and psychological impact
A reduced ability to enjoy the life you had before the accident
Loss of activities, hobbies, or relationships that mattered to you

In cases where FedEx or its driver acted with particular recklessness, such as knowingly assigning a driver with a documented history of hours-of-service violations, punitive damages may also be available in addition to the above.

One factor that directly affects the final number is fault. As covered above, Colorado law distributes fault among all responsible parties, and it reduces your compensation in proportion to your share of responsibility. FedEx’s defense team will work to raise that percentage, which is why how your case is built and documented matters as much as the injuries themselves.
What to Expect When You Sue FedEx

FedEx does not approach these claims casually. Their insurers move quickly after a crash, often reaching out to injured parties before they have legal representation. Their attorneys will dispute fault, scrutinize your medical history, and seek ways to characterize their driver as an independent contractor rather than a direct employee, a common tactic to limit the corporation’s exposure. Early settlement offers tend to arrive before the full extent of injuries is understood, and accepting one too soon is a mistake that cannot be undone.
At
Dormer Harpring
, our
Denver FedEx truck accident lawyers
prepare for all of it from day one. Here is how the process typically unfolds:
Filing the Complaint:
We file suit in Colorado state court or federal court, depending on the facts of your case, and FedEx is formally served. This step signals that your claim will not be brushed aside.
Discovery:
Both sides exchange evidence. Depositions are taken from the driver, FedEx safety personnel, and expert witnesses. Black box data, driver logs, and maintenance records become central exhibits.
Motions and Pre-Trial Proceedings:
FedEx’s attorneys routinely file motions to limit evidence or challenge expert testimony. We anticipate these tactics and prepare counter-arguments well in advance.
Settlement or Trial:
Many cases resolve before a jury is seated once FedEx recognizes it is facing a prepared, experienced opposition. When a settlement is not possible, we are prepared to take the case to trial.
The reality is that FedEx settles more often when they know the other side is willing to go to court. As your
Denver FedEx truck accident lawyer
, we build every case with trial in mind from the start, and that posture is what produces better outcomes at every stage, including before a trial ever begins.

faqs.question: How is a FedEx truck accident different from a regular car accident claim?

children.text: These cases carry more complexity than a standard car accident claim. FedEx operates under federal safety regulations covering driver hours and vehicle maintenance, creating an additional layer of evidence and legal standards. The corporation also deploys rapid response teams quickly, meaning their defense begins building almost immediately. Combined with insurers experienced in handling large commercial claims, the gap between what an unrepresented victim recovers and what an attorney can secure becomes significant.

faqs.question: What evidence is most important in a FedEx truck accident case?

children.text: The most valuable evidence tends to disappear the fastest. Electronic logging device records, black box data, dashcam footage, and driver inspection reports can be overwritten within days if no preservation demand is issued. Delivery schedules, driver employment records, and internal communications about the driver’s history can also become critical to establishing negligence. Moving quickly to secure all of it is one of the most important steps a
Denver FedEx truck accident lawyer
can take early in a case.

faqs.question: Can I sue FedEx directly, or only the driver?

children.text: In most cases, you can pursue a claim against FedEx directly. When a driver operates under FedEx’s control, uses its vehicles, and follows its delivery instructions, the company can be held liable for that driver’s negligence. FedEx routinely argues that its drivers are independent contractors to limit its exposure, but that classification does not automatically hold up under scrutiny. We investigate the actual working relationship and challenge the independent contractor defense when the evidence supports doing so.

faqs.question: What if I was partially at fault for the accident?

children.text: You may still be able to recover compensation. Colorado follows a modified comparative negligence rule, meaning an injured person can recover damages as long as their share of fault is below 50 percent. Your total compensation is reduced by your percentage of fault. FedEx’s defense team will work to increase that percentage, which is why thorough documentation and strong legal representation matter from the start.

faqs.question: What does it cost to hire a Denver FedEx truck accident lawyer?

children.text: Nothing upfront. We handle these cases on a contingency fee basis, which means you pay no legal fees unless we recover compensation for you. We also advance the costs of expert witnesses and case expenses without charging interest. You can focus entirely on your recovery without worrying about legal bills accumulating while your case is pending.

faqs.question: Will my case go to trial?

children.text: Most cases resolve before trial, but not because going to trial is off the table. Cases that settle fairly almost always do so because the injured party’s legal team was fully prepared to try the case in court. FedEx and its insurers are far more likely to negotiate seriously when they know the opposition is ready and willing to let a jury decide. We build every case with trial in mind, which puts our clients in the strongest possible position at every stage of the process.

faqs.question: How long do I have to file a claim in Colorado?

children.text: Colorado’s general statute of limitations for personal injury claims is three years from the date of the accident. While three years may seem like ample time, waiting works against you. Evidence is lost, witnesses become harder to locate, and FedEx’s defense team continues building its case in the meantime. Speaking with a
Denver FedEx truck accident lawyer
early gives your case the strongest foundation.
